newsitem.title: ANGOLA: No sign of Rwanda refugees near Angola - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: No sign of Rwanda refugees near Angola - Red Cross.

text.p: No evidence has been found of 30,000 Rwandan refugees reported last week to be approaching Angola from neighbouring Zaire, an International Red Cross official said on Monday.

Last week officials from the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) in Geneva quoted unconfirmed Zairean reports of 30,000 Rwandan refugees, among them soldiers of Rwanda's former Hutu-led government, headed towards the Angolan border.

The Red Cross official said a team of Red Cross and UNHCR relief workers spoke with local government administrators and members of a United Nations peacekeeping force in Angola's extreme north-west Lunda Northe Province.
"The team has returned to Luanda and they have not found anything. At this time we cannot confirm that these refugees are there," the Red Cross official said.
The relief team also met with government officials and aid workers in the western province of Moxico.

Thousands of Hutus fled the Tingi-Tingi refugee camp in eastern Zaire in March when rebels led by Laurent Kabila, fighting to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko's 32-year regime, approached the camp.
